body:
On Apple Silicon macOS `int(INF)` return `9223372036854775807`, `int(-INF)` return `-9223372036854775808`, and `int(NAN)` return `0`. Most likely it is difference between ARM and x86.

Since it is undefined behavior, I would omit any specific values in the docs, since technically it can return anything.

body:
Also, it's not limited to an INF / NAN, casting any value that is outside 64-bit signed integer range is UB, since it is UB in C++:

> 6.3.1.4 Real floating and integer
>
> When a finite value of real floating type is converted to an integer type other than _Bool, the
fractional part is discarded (i.e., the value is truncated toward zero). If the value of the integral part
cannot be represented by the integer type, the behavior is undefined.

It might be worth mentioning somewhere in the docs, but not sure what would be an appropriate place for it.

body:
It still mentions it depends on the platform, not what @AThousandShips was requesting.

In my opinion, too, it's not ideal to mention it in the documentation.

The "specifics" are, in fact, best left to the imagination because, by definition, "undefined behavior" cannot be relied on. The underlying hardware, OS, browser(?), or even the engine may change this behavior at any time by virtue of being undefined, at which point "platform-dependent" is too vague, but still gives the wrong idea that it's somehow possible handle this behavior per-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS, web, Android, etc.)
